why: Comtech's own announcement: Q4 and fiscal 2026 results after the close on Wed 2026-10-14, call at 17:00 ET. Stocktwits' 'Sep 29 pre-market' row is a stale vendor projection.
session_evidence: Company release: results after market close 2026-10-14, call 5:00 p.m. ET (https://finviz.com/news/401002/comtech-to-host-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2026-earnings-conference-call)
where_to_look: The status of the Gilat sale of the satellite and space segment ($157.5m, close expected calendar Q4 2026, subject to regulatory review): any CFIUS or other regulatory progress, and whether it slips. Check the 8-Ks after 2026-06-15 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000023197/000110465926073803/tm2617923d1_ex99-1.htm)

The credit-facility amendment and the replacement convertible preferred: covenant levels, the 65% mandatory paydown, preferred terms and dilution. A $39m equity cap sits under that capital stack, so the financing trail is where the value lives
Liquidity was $49.4m at Q3 with a 0.67x book-to-bill. Look at the 10-K's going-concern language and the liquidity disclosure
Allerium (public safety, NG911) contract awards and state 911 procurement wins or losses since June. The Q3 Allerium book-to-bill was 0.32x
already_in_the_wire: The Gilat divestiture terms and the pivot and rename to Allerium (June 15 2026)
Q3 FY26: sales $106.0m below consensus, non-GAAP loss of $0.22 better than the -$0.27 consensus, backlog $696.1m
The stock fell ~37.8% in the month after the Q3 print and is -78.8% from its 52-week high
trades_on: Revenue, bookings and balance-sheet news rather than EPS. The Q3 FY26 print beat on the loss line but missed on revenue, had weak Allerium book-to-bill and announced the Gilat sale the same day, and the stock fell 42.9% (https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/comtech-reports-narrower-expected-q3-loss-despite-lower-revenues). Six of seven baseline reactions were negative, median |18.1%|.
